name: London transport bombings
description: Coordinated terrorist bombs hit the London Underground and a bus during rush hour, killing 52 people and briefly shaking European markets and sterling.

name: Hurricane Katrina
description: Hurricane Katrina makes landfall near New Orleans, shutting most US Gulf of Mexico oil production and many refineries and pushing fuel prices to record highs.

name: May 2006 emerging market selloff
description: Inflation fears and further Federal Reserve rate hikes trigger a sharp global selloff in emerging market stocks, commodities and other risky assets.

name: Israel-Lebanon war 2006
description: War breaks out between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon, raising fears of wider Middle East conflict and pushing oil prices to new highs.

name: Shanghai stock crash 2007
description: Chinese stocks fall about 9% in one day on fears of a government crackdown on speculation, setting off a global stock market sell-off.

name: BNP Paribas freezes funds
description: BNP Paribas freezes three investment funds exposed to US subprime mortgages, saying it cannot value them; interbank lending markets seize up and the ECB injects emergency cash.

name: Northern Rock bank run
description: British mortgage lender Northern Rock asks the Bank of England for emergency funding, triggering the first run on a UK bank in over a century.

name: Fed first cut of the 2007 crisis
description: The Federal Reserve cuts interest rates by half a percentage point, more than expected, to contain damage from the subprime mortgage crisis.

name: Fed emergency cut January 2008
description: After a global stock rout, the Federal Reserve makes an emergency three-quarter-point rate cut between meetings, its largest single cut in decades.

name: Bear Stearns rescue
description: Investment bank Bear Stearns, hit by mortgage losses and a run by its lenders, is sold to JPMorgan for a fraction of its value with Federal Reserve support.

name: Oil peaks near $147
description: Oil prices hit a record near $147 a barrel on strong demand and tight supply, squeezing consumers and raising inflation fears worldwide.

name: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac takeover
description: The US government places mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac into conservatorship, taking control of firms backing about half of US home loans.

name: Lehman Brothers bankruptcy
description: Lehman Brothers files for the largest bankruptcy in US history after no rescue is found; Merrill Lynch is sold and insurer AIG needs a government bailout days later.

name: House rejects TARP bailout
description: The US House of Representatives votes down the $700 billion bank rescue plan, and stocks suffer one of their largest one-day falls in history.

name: Coordinated global rate cuts
description: The Federal Reserve, ECB, Bank of England and other central banks make an unprecedented joint emergency interest rate cut as the financial crisis deepens.

name: Fed launches QE1
description: The Federal Reserve announces it will buy hundreds of billions of dollars of mortgage-backed securities and agency debt, the start of quantitative easing.

name: Fed cuts rates to zero
description: The Federal Reserve cuts its policy rate to a range of zero to 0.25% and promises to use all tools to support the economy.

name: March 2009 market bottom
description: After months of bank failures and recession, Citigroup says it was profitable early in the year, sparking a powerful rally from the lows of the financial crisis.

name: Fed buys Treasuries in QE1
description: The Federal Reserve expands quantitative easing and says it will buy up to $300 billion of long-term US government bonds, sending yields sharply lower.

name: US bank stress test results
description: US regulators publish stress test results for the 19 largest banks, showing manageable capital needs and restoring confidence in the banking system.

name: Greece downgraded to junk
description: Standard & Poor's cuts Greece's credit rating to junk and downgrades Portugal, intensifying fears of a European sovereign debt crisis.

name: Flash Crash
description: US stocks plunge nearly 10% within minutes before recovering, as automated trading and a large sell order cause a sudden collapse in market liquidity.

name: EU-IMF euro rescue fund
description: European leaders and the IMF agree a rescue package of about 750 billion euros and the ECB starts buying government bonds to stop the euro debt crisis spreading.

name: Fed announces QE2
description: The Federal Reserve announces a second round of quantitative easing, buying $600 billion of US government bonds to support a weak recovery.

name: Ireland requests bailout
description: Ireland asks the European Union and IMF for a bailout after losses at its banks overwhelm the government's finances.

name: Egypt revolution
description: Mass protests spread across Egypt in the Arab Spring, raising fears for the Suez Canal and Middle East oil supplies.

name: Libya civil war cuts oil
description: Civil war in Libya halts most of the country's oil exports, pushing oil prices sharply higher.

name: Japan earthquake and Fukushima
description: A massive earthquake and tsunami hit Japan, causing a nuclear disaster at Fukushima and disrupting global supply chains.

name: Commodity crash May 2011
description: Commodity prices collapse, with oil falling about 10% in a day and silver crashing, as speculators exit crowded positions.

name: IEA emergency oil release
description: The International Energy Agency announces a coordinated release of emergency oil stocks to offset lost Libyan supply.

name: US credit rating downgrade
description: Standard & Poor's strips the United States of its top AAA credit rating after a bitter debt ceiling fight, and global stocks plunge as investors seek safety.

name: Fed Operation Twist
description: The Federal Reserve announces Operation Twist, selling short-term bonds to buy long-term ones, and warns of significant downside risks to the economy.

name: Central banks cut dollar funding cost
description: Major central banks jointly make US dollar loans cheaper for banks to ease funding stress caused by the euro crisis.

name: Greek debt restructuring
description: Greece completes the largest sovereign debt restructuring in history, with private bondholders accepting large losses.

name: Spain bank bailout request
description: Spain requests up to 100 billion euros of European aid to recapitalise its banks hit by a property crash.

name: Draghi whatever it takes
description: ECB President Mario Draghi pledges to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro, calming the European debt crisis.

name: Fed launches QE3
description: The Federal Reserve launches open-ended bond purchases of $40 billion a month until the job market improves substantially.

name: US fiscal cliff deal
description: US lawmakers pass a last-minute deal avoiding automatic tax rises and spending cuts known as the fiscal cliff.

name: Cyprus deposit levy
description: Cyprus's bailout plan proposes a levy on bank deposits; banks close and capital controls follow, shaking confidence in euro area deposits.

name: Gold crash April 2013
description: Gold suffers its biggest two-day fall in decades as investors abandon it on hopes of recovery and fears of central bank sales.

name: Taper tantrum
description: Fed Chair Ben Bernanke says bond purchases could be slowed, triggering a sharp rise in bond yields and emerging market selling.

name: US government shutdown 2013
description: The US federal government shuts down for over two weeks in a budget fight, raising fears of a debt default.

name: Fed announces taper
description: The Federal Reserve announces it will start reducing its monthly bond purchases, ending the expansion of quantitative easing.

name: Mt. Gox collapse
description: Mt. Gox, then the largest bitcoin exchange, goes offline after losing hundreds of thousands of customers' bitcoins to theft.

name: Russia takes Crimea
description: Russian forces take control of Ukraine's Crimea peninsula, sparking the worst East-West crisis since the Cold War and the threat of sanctions.

name: OPEC refuses to cut output
description: OPEC decides not to cut production despite a glut, choosing to defend market share against US shale, and oil prices plunge.

name: Swiss franc cap removed
description: The Swiss National Bank unexpectedly scraps its cap on the franc, which jumps about 30% in minutes, causing large losses at brokers.

name: ECB launches QE
description: The European Central Bank announces large-scale government bond purchases of 60 billion euros a month to fight deflation.

name: Greek capital controls
description: Greece closes its banks and imposes capital controls after talks with creditors collapse and a referendum on bailout terms is called.

name: China devalues yuan
description: China unexpectedly devalues the yuan, raising fears of a sharper Chinese slowdown and a global currency war.

name: China Black Monday 2015
description: Chinese stocks crash and global markets plunge at the open, with the Dow briefly falling 1,000 points on fears about China's economy.

name: Fed first hike since 2006
description: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time in nearly a decade, ending the era of zero rates.

name: China circuit breaker turmoil
description: Chinese stocks trigger new circuit breakers and trading halts at the start of 2016, starting a global sell-off alongside falling oil.

name: Oil falls below $30
description: Oil falls to a 12-year low below $30 a barrel on a global glut and Iran's return to export markets after sanctions.

name: Brexit vote
description: The United Kingdom votes to leave the European Union in a surprise referendum result; sterling crashes and global stocks fall.

name: Bitfinex hack
description: Crypto exchange Bitfinex is hacked and about 120,000 bitcoins are stolen, halting trading and hitting bitcoin's price.

name: Trump wins 2016 election
description: Donald Trump wins the US presidency in a surprise result; investors bet on tax cuts and spending, lifting stocks, yields and the dollar.

name: OPEC agrees output cut 2016
description: OPEC agrees its first production cut since 2008, later joined by Russia, to support oil prices.

name: North Korea fire and fury
description: Tensions with North Korea escalate as the US president threatens fire and fury, prompting a move into safe-haven assets.

name: China bans ICOs
description: China bans initial coin offerings and soon orders domestic crypto exchanges to close, hitting cryptocurrency prices.

name: Bitcoin bubble peak 2017
description: Bitcoin peaks near $20,000 as CME launches bitcoin futures at the height of a speculative mania, followed by a long crash.

name: Volmageddon
description: US stocks drop sharply and volatility explodes as products betting on calm markets collapse, after strong wage data raises inflation fears.

name: US-China tariffs begin
description: The US announces tariffs on up to $60 billion of Chinese imports, starting a trade war with China.

name: October 2018 rate scare
description: US stocks fall sharply as 10-year yields reach multi-year highs and the Fed signals continued tightening.

name: Crypto crash November 2018
description: Bitcoin breaks below $6,000 and crypto prices collapse during a dispute over the Bitcoin Cash hard fork.

name: Fed hikes into selloff 2018
description: The Federal Reserve raises rates and signals more tightening despite falling markets, deepening a December stock market slide.

name: Powell pivot to patience
description: Fed Chair Jerome Powell says the Fed will be patient and flexible on rates, and stocks rally strongly.

name: Tariff escalation May 2019
description: The US president announces higher tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods, reigniting the trade war.

name: Fed first cut since 2008
description: The Federal Reserve cuts rates for the first time since the financial crisis, citing trade tensions and weak global growth.

name: Yuan breaks 7 per dollar
description: China lets the yuan weaken past 7 per dollar and the US labels China a currency manipulator, escalating the trade war.

name: Abqaiq drone attack
description: Drone and missile attacks hit Saudi Arabia's Abqaiq oil processing plant, briefly knocking out about half of Saudi oil output.

name: US repo market spike
description: Overnight funding rates in the US repo market spike to 10%, forcing the Federal Reserve to inject cash for the first time in a decade.

name: US kills Soleimani
description: A US strike kills Iranian general Qassem Soleimani, raising fears of war in the Middle East.

name: Wuhan lockdown
description: China locks down the city of Wuhan and nearby cities, home to millions of people, to contain a new coronavirus outbreak.

name: COVID spreads to Europe
description: Coronavirus cases surge in Italy and beyond, and global markets begin their fastest crash in history as a pandemic becomes likely.

name: Fed emergency cut March 2020
description: The Federal Reserve makes an emergency half-point rate cut between meetings to counter the coronavirus.

name: Saudi-Russia oil price war
description: Saudi Arabia launches an oil price war after talks with Russia collapse, and oil prices crash about 25% in one day during the pandemic.

name: Fed cuts to zero COVID
description: The Federal Reserve cuts rates to zero and restarts massive bond buying on a Sunday, but stocks still crash on pandemic lockdowns.

name: Fed unlimited QE
description: The Federal Reserve announces unlimited bond purchases and its first corporate bond buying programme, marking the bottom of the COVID crash.

name: Oil goes negative
description: US oil futures fall below zero for the first time as storage fills up during pandemic lockdowns.

name: COVID second wave fears
description: US stocks fall about 6% in one day on fears of a second coronavirus wave and a gloomy Federal Reserve outlook.

name: Fed average inflation targeting
description: The Federal Reserve adopts average inflation targeting, signalling it will keep rates low even if inflation runs above 2% for a while.

name: US election 2020
description: Joe Biden wins the US presidential election after a close count, removing a source of uncertainty for markets.

name: Pfizer vaccine breakthrough
description: Pfizer and BioNTech announce a coronavirus vaccine about 90% effective, sparking a huge rotation into economically sensitive stocks.

name: GameStop short squeeze
description: Retail traders drive a massive short squeeze in GameStop and other stocks, forcing hedge funds to cover and brokers to restrict trading.

name: Tesla buys bitcoin
description: Tesla discloses a $1.5 billion bitcoin purchase and plans to accept it as payment, boosting cryptocurrency prices.

name: Archegos collapse
description: Family office Archegos Capital defaults on margin calls, forcing banks into fire sales and causing billions in losses at Credit Suisse and Nomura.

name: Crypto crash May 2021
description: Cryptocurrencies crash as China warns against crypto use and Tesla stops accepting bitcoin over energy concerns.

name: Evergrande default fears
description: Fears that heavily indebted Chinese property developer Evergrande will default trigger a global stock sell-off.

name: US inflation hits 6.2%
description: US consumer prices rise 6.2% from a year earlier, the fastest in three decades, raising pressure on the Fed to tighten.

name: Omicron variant
description: A new heavily mutated coronavirus variant, Omicron, is identified, and markets fall sharply on fears of new lockdowns.

name: Fed signals balance sheet runoff
description: Federal Reserve minutes show officials want to raise rates sooner and shrink the balance sheet, triggering a sell-off in growth stocks.

name: Russia invades Ukraine
description: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine; Western sanctions follow and energy and food prices surge.

name: Fed first hike 2022
description: The Federal Reserve raises rates for the first time since 2018 and signals a series of hikes to fight high inflation.

name: Terra Luna collapse
description: The TerraUSD stablecoin loses its dollar peg and its sister token Luna collapses to almost zero, wiping out about $40 billion.

name: Celsius freezes withdrawals
description: Crypto lender Celsius freezes customer withdrawals, deepening a crypto crash as hot US inflation data hits markets.

name: Fed 75bp hike
description: The Federal Reserve raises rates by three-quarters of a point, its biggest hike since 1994, to fight 40-year-high inflation.

name: Powell Jackson Hole 2022
description: Fed Chair Powell warns that fighting inflation will bring pain to households and businesses, ending a summer stock rally.

name: UK mini-budget gilt crisis
description: The UK government announces large unfunded tax cuts; gilt yields spike, sterling crashes and pension funds face margin calls until the Bank of England intervenes.

name: FTX collapse
description: Crypto exchange FTX halts withdrawals after a run by customers and files for bankruptcy, revealing misuse of client funds.

name: US inflation cools November 2022
description: US inflation comes in lower than expected, and stocks surge over 5% in a day on hopes the Fed will slow its rate hikes.

name: Silicon Valley Bank failure
description: Silicon Valley Bank collapses after a deposit run triggered by bond losses, the largest US bank failure since 2008; Signature Bank follows.

name: Credit Suisse rescue
description: Swiss authorities force UBS to take over Credit Suisse in an emergency deal, wiping out some of its bonds.

name: First Republic seized
description: First Republic Bank is seized by regulators and sold to JPMorgan, the second-largest bank failure in US history.

name: US debt ceiling deal 2023
description: US leaders agree a deal to suspend the debt ceiling, averting a possible default by the Treasury.

name: Fitch downgrades US
description: Fitch Ratings cuts the US credit rating from AAA to AA+, citing fiscal deterioration and repeated debt limit standoffs.

name: Hamas attack on Israel
description: Hamas launches a surprise attack on Israel, which declares war, raising fears of a wider Middle East conflict.

name: 10-year yield nears 5%
description: The US 10-year Treasury yield approaches 5%, its highest since 2007, as markets price higher-for-longer rates and large deficits.

name: Fed pivot December 2023
description: The Federal Reserve signals it expects to cut rates in the coming year, sparking a rally in bonds and stocks.

name: Spot bitcoin ETFs approved
description: The US SEC approves the first spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds, opening bitcoin to mainstream investors.

name: BOJ ends negative rates
description: The Bank of Japan raises rates for the first time in 17 years, ending the world's last negative interest rate policy.

name: Iran attacks Israel 2024
description: Iran launches hundreds of drones and missiles at Israel in its first direct attack, raising fears of regional war.

name: CrowdStrike outage
description: A faulty CrowdStrike software update crashes millions of Windows computers, grounding flights and disrupting banks and hospitals worldwide.

name: Yen carry trade unwind
description: Japanese stocks crash 12% in a day as a Bank of Japan hike and weak US jobs data force investors to unwind yen-funded trades.

name: Fed 50bp cut 2024
description: The Federal Reserve starts cutting rates with a half-point reduction as inflation cools and the job market softens.

name: Trump wins 2024 election
description: Donald Trump wins the 2024 US election; markets price tax cuts, tariffs and deregulation, lifting stocks, the dollar and bitcoin.

name: DeepSeek AI shock
description: Chinese startup DeepSeek releases a cheap high-performing AI model, and US AI and chip stocks plunge, with Nvidia losing about $600 billion in value.

name: Bybit hack
description: Crypto exchange Bybit loses about $1.5 billion of ether in the largest crypto theft ever, attributed to North Korean hackers.

name: Liberation Day tariffs
description: The US announces sweeping tariffs on almost all trading partners, far larger than expected, and global stocks crash with US bonds and the dollar also falling.

name: Tariff pause rally
description: The US pauses most new tariffs for 90 days, and US stocks jump about 9.5% in one of their best days ever.

name: Israel strikes Iran
description: Israel launches large air strikes on Iran's nuclear and military sites, and oil prices jump on fears for Gulf supply.

name: US strikes Iran nuclear sites
description: The United States bombs Iranian nuclear facilities; Iran's limited response and a quick ceasefire send oil prices back down.

name: October 2025 crypto liquidation
description: A threat of 100% US tariffs on China triggers a sell-off and the largest liquidation of leveraged crypto positions on record.
